newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-TENTATIVE BECKER RELIES ON BIG SERVE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-TENTATIVE BECKER RELIES ON BIG SERVE.

text.p: It was the same old game plan, but minus the tumbling volleys and precision placement, as former champion Boris Becker exorcised his recent tormented past at Wimbledon to breeze into the second round on Tuesday.

Becker, a crowd favourite here since becoming the youngest player to lift the men's singles title at 17 years and seven months in 1984, relied on his powerful service game to brush past Spanish baseliner Marcos Aurilio Gorriz 6-3 6-2 6-3.

The sharp edge to Becker's game has been blunted over the past year since his painful retirement at Wimbledon in 1996, and the high octane levels which have carried to him three Wimbledon titles over the past 13 years was turned off on Tuesday.
But the German, who was honoured at the opening of the new number one court on Monday as one of Wimbledon's great players, said he was happy with his performance.
"The first round is usually a bit more difficult because everything is just so new, but I made sure I had a good start," said Becker.
Twelve months ago the German's dream of winning a fourth Wimbledon title was shattered by a ruptured right wrist in the third round prompting a cautionary start to this year's tournament.
Court two is known as the 'graveyard', but Becker said court one had provided his worst moments and admitted he was pleased to see it reduced to rubble this year.
"My problem usually was old number one court, so I'm kind of glad they put it down because I have broken my wrist there," he said. "I also had the longest matches in the tournament there.
"Court number two I once had bad match, which was a long time ago, but ever since that match I have not lost on it. So for me it's not a graveyard."
The acrobatic net skills of past years were virtually non-existent on Tuesday, the German eighth seed hitting the turf on only one occasion while his trademark drop volleys were few and far between.
Becker's serve was largely on target from the start as he dropped only two points in his opening three service games.

He then took the initiative in the eighth game breaking Gorriz, ranked a lowly 173 in the world, with one of his only two volley winners in the first set. He picked up another break in the ninth game, pouncing on the Spaniard's short, soft second serve to take the set in 29 minutes.

Becker, who has dipped to 18 in the world rankings after his injury-plagued last 12 months, grew in confidence in the second set, approaching the net more regularly to hit seven winners and secure two breaks of serve.
The German broke his rival in the sixth game of the third set and hammered a backhand past Gorriz to clinch the match in one hour and 42 minutes.
"I think, as long as I'm in tennis in a very competitive way I have a chance at Wimbledon," he said.
"It depends on the draw, depends on the weather, many things, but the grasscourt game is very natural to me and once I get going I feel like I have a chance against to play well against anybody."
Becker will next meet either Dominik Hrbaty of Slovakia or Thomas Johansson of Sweden.
